recs.name: Fins on the Night Desert
recs.tag: Did you see that, sandbeast? The legend about fins on the night desert is real, and it's got to do with you and me.

lines.x: Hurry up! It's already 13:00! As soon as we finish lunch we need to start cooking! Golden carrots must be first on the list! Trust me. It's not a real feast without golden carrots!

Where are the plates? There aren't enough plates here! Where are the bowls? And we'll need at least twenty more tables, and chairs! My thirteenth uncle's second aunt came too, and she's bringing her five little kids. How exciting!
Hey! The whole reason I came here was to cook for you! So what if I'm a guest? Are you seriously not going to let me cook? Hurry up and hand me the spatula!
Wraw!
Come here, Sandbeast.
You're not afraid of all this noise? You... like it?
Wraw! Wraw!
Hey, Jerry, look! I see Ray over there!
Oh! Hey, Ray! We're over here!
Is someone calling me?
—over here!
Oh, Jerry! It's you!
I'm so sorry. There are just so many people here. I yelled as loud as I possibly could!
After Keira and I got back from our honeymoon, I wanted to throw a thank-you party for you. Then somehow the guest list just kept growing... Still, I'm really happy with how it turned out!
Because no one here would have thought that Keira and I would end up together, after we both ran away from the altar...
Jerry... It's awfully noisy here. I can't hear what you're saying!
Can you speak a bit louder?

(Takes a deep breath)
I SAID...
THAT KEIRA AND I...
ARE VERY GLAD YOU COULD MAKE IT!
Okay. I heard you that time!
Oh—and I have to say, Keira and I both think that if you hadn't been there, so much of what followed wouldn't even have happened!
That's right!

Keira and I wouldn't have ended up running away and then meeting like that! We wouldn't have gotten to know each other so quickly! And everything else that happened afterward... WE TRULY HAVE TO THANK YOU!
Ah. I heard that too!
Did I make that much of a difference, really?
OF—COURSE!
If you hadn't hijacked the truck, maybe Keira and I would never have met up! Who knows when or if I'd have my family pushing me down another path.
That is why we're so grateful to you, Ray!
THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR THE HIJACKING!!!
Hijacking? Did you hear that? Did I get the word wrong?
I remember Jerry said he was carjacked. They crashed through the checkpoint and had a fight with the guard. That was all her doing?
What? I can't hear you! You're saying that she stole Jerry away?
What? It's too noisy! You're saying she jacked the truck... for Jerry?!
What?! She crashed through the checkpoint and had a fight with the guard, only to hijack the truck and take Jerry away?!
WHAT?!
Sorry, Ray, but we still have so much to do. Do you still remember where you're sitting?
Yes. Pavilion 3, near the geyser, table 12, seat 6.
Warmy will be to the left of you, and Alanna to the right. There's also a wooden crate there for your sandbeast.
Right.
Ray, you just have to try our cooking tonight! OKAY! See you later!
Sure!
Wraw!
(Happily stretches its backfin)
(Happily digs into the sand)
Now, sandbeast. This isn't your personal playground. You can't behave like that.
Wraw! Wraw! Wraw! Wraw!
You've been so hyper ever since we got back to Rim Billiton.
...Sandbeast.
I've saved up a bit of money. We don't have to work tomorrow. Let me take you out to the wilderness for a little while right now.
I know you want to go run in the wilds, dig tunnels, and play with the sand.
Look! It's right over there. I'll stay here and build us a little shelter. You go on ahead. I'll keep an eye on you.
Wraw!
Wraw! Wraw—wraw!
Sandbeast, let's go out and play while we have the chance.
Long ago I took a sandbeast, my first sandbeast, to the wilderness to play.
It was so happy, as happy as you are now.
(Points out the window towards the wilderness)
Let's go have some fun, yeah?
(Rubs excitedly)
First we'll go get a map, and then we'll find you some snacks. Then we'll borrow Lanns's car.
Let's go!
Has that girl been talking to the sandbeast ever since Jerry and Keira left?
She jacked a truck so she could take Jerry away...
She looks like she's in bad shape...
Huh? Look... she left already? She doesn't even want to stay for the meal?
That doesn't seem right. I think you lot should follow her. Don't leave her alone!
I've been following her from a distance, don't worry. After she left, she went straight to that little shop outside town—probably to buy something.
Yup. I saw her walk in there. Don't worry. I'll go over there and get a few more groceries. What do you all need?
Cystymilk, onions, cheese... okay, got it.
Lanns said it was here, from what I remember... preserved corpses, skeletons, photographs...
Here's the place. Easy.
Hello? Is anyone here? I'd like a map showing the locations of large sandbeast caves nearby.
Huh? Who are you? Maps? You came here for 'Fins on the Night Desert' too?
I heard that legend before, but that's not why I'm here.
Then why are you here? What do you all think this is, a wishing well that anyone can stop by?
I'm a pitsinker. These are my old work credentials, medical report, and attendance records… If you help me, I can take you to any abandoned mine or underground cave you want to visit.
What do you think about that?
Now that's new—never seen anyone like you, coming here like you're applying for a job or something. Alright, let me take a look...
Wraw!
Oh? You actually managed to tame that little thing?
No. It just followed me here on its own.
Followed you here? Huh. Interesting.
This is... a Rhodes Island dining card? You're from Rhodes Island?
Yes.
Alright—you've worked as a pitsinker, you can tame a sandbeast, and you're a Rhodes Island operator... If the Doctor picked you, you must have some skills. Here, take the map.
Leave me your contact. Next time I want to explore a cave, I'll contact you.
Alright. I've finished my shopping. Let me see where she is... huh? Wait a minute, she... what is she going to that shop for? Is that... an animal carcass... and is that a corpse?
No. There's just no way I can let her stay in that kind of place by herself. I need to go see what's going on! Oh this is awful!
Hey! Unhand my guest!
Wha? What now? Where did you come from?
Whoa? Huh? Where is she? Where did she go?
Dammit! I lost track of her!
Don't worry. I was on my way back from rinsing out some old barbecue barrels in the mines, and I saw her coming right this way after I got your message.
Yes, she was there with the sandbeast. I'm sure you'll see her in another ten minutes or so.
You still need four more barbecue barrels, huh? Alright. I'll bring them over right away!
Sandbeast, look over there. We've found what we were looking for.
The mushrooms and moss that grow in the mine tunnels... they're tasty and good for your health. They can help sandbeasts purge toxins.
Wraw.
Well, today you can eat a little less feed and instead snack on some moss and mushrooms. Think of it as 'picnic food'!
Come with me. We'll go find some.
Wraw!
Sandbeast, hold on to me tight. We're about to head down.
Wraw!
Hey! Hey! What are you doing?!
Uh oh. I've got some bad news. I was just finishing brushing one of the barrels when I saw her go down into the mine!
To make matters worse, it's an abandoned mine. I don't dare go in there myself. I'll stand guard at the entrance until she comes back up!
I heard a sound coming from up above us. Did you hear it, Sandbeast?
Munchmunch...
Wraw?
Maybe it was the wind.
Hey. Don't eat so much. We need to bring some moss and mushrooms back with us, you know.
If you eat so much that we exceed the lift's weight limit, we won't be able to get back up there.
Twenty minutes later...
*burp*
Good. Let out another burp, and maybe we'll still be able to use the lift.
Wraw! Wraw!
*burp*
Okay. Great. Grab on tight. We're gonna go back up now.

Now we have only one thing left to do. We're going to ask Lanns if we can borrow her truck.
Huff...
We still have enough time left.
Lanns, I want to borrow your ute.
Huh? Why? You're travelling?
You're not going to the banquet, Ray? I made my sweet meat soup!
It's not that. I just suddenly have the urge to take Sandbeast out for a stroll.
I'll be back before the banquet starts.
You sure you'll come back?
Yes. Last time I left the ship to watch the burdenbeasts dancing under the moon, I got in trouble.
The HR Operator said next time I have to report in first, to avoid interrupting everyone's work.
You told me that before I make a decision, I need to stop and think about it first.
Ray stops for a second and thinks about it.
Well I've thought about this one. Jerry and Keira keep telling me how much they want to thank me. If I don't come back for the banquet, they'll be very hurt.
So... I'll definitely be back.
Ray finishes speaking. She looks as if she's finally figured out the answer to a major question, and she gives a small nod to herself.
Yes. I'll come back for the banquet.
Wow. I never thought you'd actually remember what I told you! Alright then. Here are the keys. Be careful out there.
Right, Ray, well, you have to try my sweet meat soup at the banquet, yeah?
Of course. I will.
Alright then. I'd best be going.
*huff huff* I finally finished greeting each and every guest, and arranging all their seats... I'm exhausted!
Well, let's take a little break...
It feels so good now that I've gotten all that done...
Help! Something terrible happened!
What?
No no no... We lost her! Who here has seen that quiet Cautus girl?
I watched her go into this horrifying hut—it was full of bones and corpses, and the woman inside looked terrifying. I have no idea what happened to her in there!

After Ninth Auntie lost track of her, she immediately sent us a message. I happened to see her nearby, but I was a step too late—she went straight into an abandoned mine shaft. I called for her over and over, but no one answered!
Huh? That can't be right. I just saw her here. She was driving a truck, heading over that way!
Who? Which way?
Sixth Uncle points his finger at the window.
Everyone looks over towards the window—a trail of dust gradually fades into the horizon.
She was heading south. There aren't any mines or villages over there because of all the sandbeast burrows. It's kind of a no-man's land. Is she... in trouble? Does she have a death wish or something?
Wha?
Jerry, she hijacked a truck for you before. Come on. You can't just let her run around by herself over there like that!
What?!
The sandbeasts lounge about, stirring up the sand as they slowly trudge across the boundless desert, enjoying the cool night air.
The transport vehicle comes to a stop in the distance. One woman, and one beast, jump out from it.
Look, Sandbeast. We're here.
Here. I'll rearrange your moss and mushrooms for you. There we go.
Go out and play. You'll love it.
Wraw—!
The little sandbeast lets out a joyful cry and charges into the pack up ahead. It merrily rolls around, rubbing up against all the other sandbeasts.
The pack doesn't reject the newcomer. Instead, they warmly welcome its arrival, gently nudging it and sniffing its scent.
They are all carrying the same mushrooms and moss, which occasionally emit a faint glow when they bump into each other.
Wraaaaw—
Wraw—wraw—
Wraw! Wraw!
Ray is carrying those same mushrooms and moss, and thus, emits the same occasional faint glow herself. She breathes in the fresh scent of the plants and slowly trails after the pack.
Here, Sandbeast. Eat up.
I looked these mushrooms and moss up in a book. If you eat them, the color of the veins on your back will go back to normal, and you'll feel better.
Kwh—kwh—!
Kwh...
Do you feel any better?
Sorry. I'll stay close by your side and pay more attention to your health from now on, Sandbeast, especially when we're cleansing infected creatures.
I won't let you get more than five steps away from me.
Wraw...
Wraw, wraw.
You stood up! Are you better now?
Wraw, wraw!
Oh! I'm so glad, Sandbeast!
Ray reaches out her hand and strokes the sandbeast's backfin, inspecting the color of the veins to make sure it has really recovered.
The sandbeast snuggles its head against Ray's hand and shifts into a comfortable position in her arms.
Sandbeast...
I've saved up a bit of money. We don't have to work tomorrow. Let me take you out to the wilderness for a little while right now.
I know you want to go run in the wilds, dig tunnels, and play with the sand.
Look! It's right over there. I'll stay here and build us a little shelter. You go on ahead. I'll keep an eye on you.
Wraw!
Wraw! Wraw—wraw!
The sandbeast runs off excitedly into the wilderness, but quickly turns back around and gently nudges its head against Ray's ankle.
It's almost as if it's asking her to venture with it into the wilderness.
You want me to go play with you?
Wraw!
Oh, Sandbeast! Calm down! I'm about to lose my balance here! You've spilled mushrooms and moss all over me!
Oh look. After you bump into them... they start glowing?
It's actually quite pretty.
Wraaaaw—
I guess we'll keep wearing them then.
Alright. Let's go have some fun. I'll put off building the hut for a bit.
Follow me, Sandbeast!
Wraw!
These sandbeasts... sometimes when they are digging underground, they will dig into the mines.
Is that how they learned that these mushrooms and moss... remove toxins?
The sandbeast pack, of course, aren't able to answer the Cautus's question, even though she's wearing the same mushrooms and moss that they are.
They happily jostle to and fro, lighting up the mushrooms and moss hanging from their bodies, before ravenously gulping them down.
In the darkness the pack seems to float effortlessly across the desert, like a huge school of fins swimming slowly toward the glimmering moonlight.
Ray stands there, watching them.
This is the first time I've ever seen anything like this. I guess the 'Fins on the Night Desert' is a real thing.
I guess... they were talking about sandbeasts...
And my Sandbeast.
Ray starts running... and her faint glow returns.
She catches up to the sandbeasts, like a wayward fin returning to its school.
(Whistles)
*huff* *huff* ... Sandbeast!
Sandbeast! Should I give you a proper name?
A name for my first sandbeast!
What's a good name for you?
Hmm...
Wraw?
I'll call you... 'Glowy'?
Wraw...
Don't like that name?
'Shiny'? 'Lighty'?
Wraw...
Haha. No. You don't like any of those names...
I don't think I'm too good at picking names.
Let me noodle on it a bit more...
Well you keep saying 'wraw' 'wraw'... how about I call you 'Rory' for now?
Wraw?!
Relax! Relax!
Oh come on! Jerry and Keira just explained everything to you—it was all a misunderstanding! Ray didn't hijack the ute to run off with Jerry, and she wasn't trying to commit suicide in the wilderness!
She just wanted to take her sandbeast out to have some fun. It's no big deal. You don't need to worry.
If you don't believe me, ask Potlid!
Yes. Lanns is right. Ray said she'd be back in time for the banquet.
The banquet is scheduled to start at 21:30. She still has two minutes to get here.
Is she really going to come back safely?
We really don't need to go find her?
Believe me. Ray promised me that she'd be back!
It's almost 21:30. Listen to me...
Let the banquet—begin!
*huff* I'm back.
Let me think... oh right, I'm seated at pavilion 3, near the geyser, table 12, seat 6.
Potlid is sitting to my left, and Lanns is sitting to my right. There's also a wooden crate for Rory.
Right. This is the place.
Wraw!
Wow. The barbecue smells wonderful. The stew doesn't look half bad either...
Hm?
What's wrong? No one wants to eat?
Uhh... We'd like to ask...
Go ahead.
You didn't drive that truck into the no-man's land... because you suddenly lost your marbles and wanted to do something stupid?
You didn't go into that terrifying hut to buy poison, and/or something equally awful?
You didn't have some kind of mental breakdown, get lost, and end up in that abandoned mine?
What are you all saying? Of course not!
I took it out on a picnic.
Look.
Ray holds up the sandbeast at her feet, whose belly is now full and round.
The little sandbeast fidgets just slightly.
*burp*
See! I told you!
Well, let's eat!

recs.name: Dancer Beneath the Moon
recs.tag: The light that she seeks is not at the end, but on every step forward.

lines.x: Don't mind me, little one. I might not be able to move my body, but that doesn't mean I can't budge a bit.
Since you took so much effort to come all this way, I have one more question for you.
If I am the Feranmut, if I am the light you were seeking...
Considering how far you've had to come to get here, what exactly were you hoping I would help you with?
Hiya there, mind if I ask if... you've seen Ray around?
Ray? Saw her just a minute ago!
As soon as I gave her her food, she walked off while munching out of her lunchbox...
It looked like she was chasing after a hairy little shadow. Must've been her sandbeast?
Thanks! Sorry for troubling ya!
Mind if I... *huff*... phew... Mind if I ask if you've seen Ray?
I've actually seen her a bunch of times today... I was just baffled.
While I was in the office this morning, I saw her turn that corner lots of times, and she seemed to be walking faster every time she did it.
Now that I think about it, I've seen you a lot today as well, Alanna...
Be... Because I'm looking for her!
Hah... Hah... Hoo...
A-Are you alright, Alanna?
I... I'm fine...
Hey.
Whoa—?!
What's up? Everyone on the ship's been telling me you were looking for me, so I came over.
Is that so... Been spending the whole morning looking for ya, nearly turned the entire ship over while I was at it!
...Sorry. I was taking Rory out for walkies.
(Feeble bellyflop)
Is it just me... or is your sandbeast a little plumper than before?
Wraw?
I've been busy with work lately, so I asked some friends at Logistics to feed it for a few days.
By the time I got back, Rory had become a ball.
Umm...
So that's why I'm taking it on walkies when I'm free.
Ray suddenly seems to remember something, rifling through her jacket pocket.
This month's installment... Not enough.
Here's my meal card. Take it. Call it... interest.
You seriously still on about that? I'm not here to get my money back... I just hadn't seen posts about your 'adventures' on the local forum in a while, so I wanted to see how you were doing.
Mmm. Haven't been any safety violations lately, so haven't had to sign any guarantee letters.
That's great.
(Long sigh of relief)
What is it?
If I had known it wasn't about the money, I wouldn't have hid from you.
Didn't you just say you were taking the sandbeast out for walkies—?!
I couldn't think of a good excuse.

You—?!
You—this—
dorm—it's—
completely—packed!
Wraw—!
There is only barely enough space for the two and the beast to pass between the sandbox and the door, and finally they find a little more leeway by the bed.
When did this sandbox become so big... Must get in the way whenever you're hopping in and out of the room.
Rory needs more space, while I just need somewhere to sleep.
The two of them sit side-by-side on the bed, watching the sandbeast gulp down big mouthfuls of water in the sandbox.
I remember how it always used to hide behind that rock there... Never thought I'd see the day it wouldn't be scared of me.
The people here aren't scary. The last time Rory smashed up a target, Instructor Dobermann didn't get mad. We ended up fixing it up together.
That's great. Glad to see your life slowly get back on track.
Y'know, nowadays I spend all my time in Engineering helping debug new equipment. I might be busy as a bee, but it's a thousand times better than life in the mines.
No more worries about cave-ins or how muddy the drinking water is. Three hot meals a day and a nice, clean bed to sleep in.
Not even my wildest dreams back in the mines had peaceful days like this.
Mmm. Rhodes Island is nice and calm. Got everything you can think of.
To be honest, I was worried if you were suited to life aboard at first.
But when I was out there looking for you earlier, I noticed everyone got to know you already. Hell, you're even chums now. I'm not worried anymore.
So that's why I wanna say, you can stop worrying about paying me back too. You've got a steady life now, so give some thought to the future.
Once you've gotten your sandbeast a nice den, get yourself a little something too. Don't need to keep being a cheapo, y'know...
As Alanna looks around Ray's room, she notices a poster stuck to the ceiling.
Is that... the Frontier?
An old poster from Columbia. Got it from a roadside hawker during my last mission.
The poster depicts a patch of overgrown land. Above that land, the night sky, strewn with countless twinkling stars.

I also borrowed some documentaries about the place. They talked about how different the wilds of Columbia are from Rim Billiton's, about how there's weird patterns carved into the ground, and bits of iron of all shapes and sizes flying through the sky.
If that sort of stuff exists, dancing burdenbeasts don't sound too crazy.
Ray stretches out a finger, pointing at the moon on the poster. Her finger follows along the path of its light, all the way to some place even higher in the sky.
Once I've paid you everything back, I'll start saving up.
Once I've got enough, I'll hire a car, and head out into the Columbian wilds to find those burdenbeasts.
...Still thinking about those dancing burdenbeasts, huh?
Mmm. And that ray of light.
But why?
If you want to go look for a herd of beasts that might not even exist, you'll be giving up the peaceful life you got now.
...I dunno.
But ever since I saw that light, I haven't been able to forget it. Like how a sandbeast in the desert's always searching for water.
But this ain't a desert. Sandbeasts here can get water whenever they want.
There's no bottomless mines here. Even the dingiest closet here's brighter than the pit.
Don't tell me you don't like the place, Ray?
It's not that... I really like it here. It's way better than anywhere I've stayed before.
Right, and your sandbeast likes it here too—
Hey, wait, where's it gone? It was here just a moment ago...
It must've headed out after drinkies were done...
But I just closed the door...
The sandbox's entrance faces the window. A half-open window.
Have any of you seen Ray's sandbeast?!
Nope, doesn't it normally follow her around everywhere...? W-Wait, did it wander off or something?
Let's go help her find it!
The security cams have dead zones, so can't say for sure if it's still aboard...
I'll go borrow a car to chase after it!
No good! Rhodes Island's already miles away from where it was when the thing scarpered!
No, I need to find it...
Alanna! Alanna! Some operators reported something hanging off the bridge running across the deck.
I see you're close to the site, could you help check it out and do some repairs?
The bridge across the deck...
A-Alright, got it!
Hoo... Hah...
You... Y-You get over here!
Huff... Hah... I'm beat...
My God, didn't think it'd be able to run all the way up here, especially now that it's a furry little doughball...
(Scared cry) Wraw...!
The sandbeast throws itself into Ray's arms, rubbing its fur up and down against her hands.
I'm done with this fella. Of all the places in this huge ship, no idea why it decided to climb up to the high ones.
Also I'm the one who saved the little bugger, so why's it nuzzling up to you?
*sigh* I'm gonna go make my report.
Don't rub up against me, Rory. You gotta get punished if you do something bad.
Ray grabs the sandbeast's two claws, lifting them up over its head.
(Protesting cry) Wraw!
C'mon, speak up, why'd you scarper off to somewhere so dangerous?
(Excited cry) Wraw—
Whoa, where'd that thunder come from all of a sudden?!
What is it, Ray?
...There's a reason why Rory suddenly climbed up somewhere high.
Oh yeah?
Sandbeasts in the desert are dune-climbers. Sometimes, they'd stand somewhere high up to look out for predators and feel where the wind's blowing.
When the weather's taking a turn for the worse, sandbeasts will be the first to know, which is why Rory came over here.
Even though Rhodes Island has roofs and no predators, it's still going to do what it normally does.
But I heard that with real good care, sandbeasts can actually live indoors long-term without having to go back to the desert...
You can raise one like that, but it's always gonna be thinking of heading back, to feel the winds of the wilds.
(Spirited cry) Wraw!
I know... You still think about your days out in the barrens, don't you, Ray?
...You get me?
Of course I don't! I don't know a thing about whatever that ray of light means to you, or that herd of burdenbeasts you're always talking about.
...But I know a heart like yours is the type to sorely miss things.
It's like how I love my life in Engineering, but I still have times I look back at all the beautiful sights I saw while trucking.
Since you're thinking of going, go already.
...Thanks, Lanns.
Doesn't matter if you did it for Rory or for me, thanks.
(Happy cry) Wraw!
I've got one more question, Ray—
Raindrops the size of beans start falling from the sky. The desert welcomes in the year's first sunshower.
Several months later
Operator Ray. This mission will be in a comparatively remote region of Columbia, with very few supply points.
In addition, there have been recent reports of Originium energy fluctuations of unknown origin in the area. There will be a certain amount of risk involved.
Sure. I know my way around deserts, and my sandbeast is sensitive to airflows and the temperature. It'll help out.
I know that you're very capable, and have shown exemplary performance during several prior desert rescue missions.
But I still have to warn you that this mission is a long one, a month at the very least, and comms might not be particularly steady.
Got it. I'll follow the mission brief. If comms cut out, I'll follow the route and wait at the next supply point.
That's right. I wish you all the best, Operator Ray.
Oh, right!
Hmm? Is there something else?
Thanks for volunteering for this mission. To be honest, it'll be a huge help.
...No worries.
Phew, made it just in time. I heard you were heading off on a mission today, so I rushed over to give you some grain feed I bought for your sandbeast.
(Happy cry) Wraw!
Hey, don't just nuzzle up against anyone who gives you food!
Ray—!
...Potlid?
She heard you were heading somewhere far away, so she insisted on taking some leave to see you off.
You sure picked a bad time to set off. Right now, the cafeteria's clogged up with people waiting for her to make dinner.
This here's a lunchbox for you, Ray. I heard your later missions are gonna get real tough, so I made sure to pack you extra!
Sure, thanks. I'll make sure to eat it all.
I better get going, then.
Stay safe now, and don't forget to come home.
I won't. I'll pay you back your money, with interest.
I already told you, you don't need to pay me back—!
Pffeh...
Under the setting sun, Alanna and Warmy stand by the deck railing, watching Ray's car drive off into the distance.
Ray went to go find that light and those burdenbeasts, didn't she, Lanns?
When we had just arrived at Rhodes Island, she'd always tell me those stories. I thought she made them up just to make me happy.
Of course she believes in them too. She's not the kind of girl to tell fibs.
I'm really excited to hear all the new stories she'll have.
Same here. Let's wait for her and give them a listen when she's back.
(Loudly) I still got one more question—
(Loudly) You ever thought there's a chance you already found that ray of light?
(Loudly) Maybe you already saw that light a second time in your life, but your memory's all fogged up, so you never realized!
(Even louder) Well, the chase itself is pretty fun too!
Ray's mind wanders for a moment.
She turns her head to look back at the slowly-shrinking landship, a memory from what seems to be many years ago welling up.
On the day that she was rescued, there was a shadow as huge as a mountain, shooting rays of light through the fog.
And now, on top of that colossal ship, amidst layer upon layer of twilit clouds, stand her friends.
It is the place that she wants to leave, and the place that she will return to.
(Cry of freedom) Wraw!
The sandbeast's cry pulls Ray back to reality. She returns her gaze to the road ahead.
No need to rush, Rory. Heading there, looking about, just do it all slow and steady.
Doesn't matter if we don't find anything, as long as we keep up the search.
Ray drives past the dunes, speeding towards the depths of the barrens.
The setting sun behind her slowly falls, while the moons in front of her slowly rise. As she watches the moonlight, a lot of things come to mind.
She thinks of the herd of burdenbeasts that welcome the moonlight with dance. She thinks of Rory, looking out into the distance from on high.
She thinks of herself, always searching, always chasing.
